mainTopic: What kind of holiness does leftover incense have, and how can it be redeemed? The debate between רבה and רב חסדא, and רבה's idea that the בית דין makes a silent condition.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב חסדא's claim that leftover incense can be redeemed because it has only קדושת דמים, holiness tied to its value. רבה challenges him with a ברייתא saying that once incense is placed in the mortar, a טבול יום disqualifies it. He then uses a משנה about מנחות to show that value-holiness alone is not disqualified by a טבול יום, so incense must have more than קדושת דמים. רב חסדא pushes back with another משנה, which names the incense itself. If the incense had קדושת הגוף, it should also be disqualified by being left overnight, yet that משנה ties לינה to being made holy in a vessel. רבה answers that incense is different, because it never spoils, so לינה proves nothing. The גמרא returns to the basic question: if the incense had real holiness, where did that holiness go when it was redeemed? רבה answers that the בית דין silently makes a condition: whatever is not needed was only holy for its value. אביי challenges this from רבה's own ruling about a male animal dedicated for its value, and רבה separates dedicating it 'for the value of an עולה' from dedicating it 'for the value of נסכים'. אביי then begins a new challenge from the lost פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Incense has only value-holiness
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his explanation: the incense can be redeemed because its holiness is only קדושת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it has only holiness of value.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב חסדא's statement from before this section, part of his question about redeeming leftover offerings. He explains why leftover incense can be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something with קדושת דמים is holy only for its money value, so it can be redeemed for money. Animal offerings are different. They have קדושת הגוף, holiness in the item itself, which cannot be redeemed away. The rest of this section attacks this claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness tied to an item's value, not to the item itself; it can be redeemed.
Holiness in the item itself, which cannot be redeemed (mentioned for contrast).
The incense burned in the בית המקדש.

steps.whyThisMatters: Every challenge that follows targets this one claim that incense is only קדושת דמים.

phrases.english: For it has only holiness of value.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב חסדא's answer from before this section. 'It' means the incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב חסדא's statement, which began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Classifies the type of holiness involved
steps.terutzMaskana: Incense has only קדושת דמים, so it can be redeemed.

steps.title: A טבול יום can disqualify incense
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks: if incense is only קדושת דמים, a טבול יום should not disqualify it. Yet a ברייתא says it is disqualified once it is put in the mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a טבול יום should not disqualify it! Why, then, does a ברייתא teach that once it is put in a mortar, a טבול יום disqualifies it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא about incense in the mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה assumes that only things with real holiness of the item itself can be disqualified by a טבול יום. The ברייתא says a טבול יום does disqualify incense in the mortar. That suggests the incense has more than value-holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if that is so…', a formula that draws an unwanted result from someone's claim.
Someone who was impure and immersed today but is not fully pure until nightfall.
A mortar, used to grind the incense.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
it should not be disqualified by a טבול יום!
Why, then, was it taught:
Once he placed it in the mortar,
it is disqualified by a טבול יום?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לֹא תִּפָּסֵל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that incense is only קדושת דמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Value-holiness alone cannot be disqualified by a טבול יום. A ברייתא says incense in the mortar is disqualified this way, so it must have more than value-holiness.

steps.title: Value-holiness alone is not disqualified by a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules out a possible defense. Someone might say that even קדושת דמים items can be disqualified by a טבול יום. A משנה about מנחות shows that only items made holy in a vessel can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that anything with holiness of value can be disqualified by a טבול יום: but we learned in a משנה that one is liable for מעילה with מנחות from when they are dedicated. Once they are made holy in a vessel, they become able to be disqualified by a טבול יום, by a מחוסר כפורים, and by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה expects a defense of רב חסדא and blocks it ahead of time. He quotes a משנה about the ingredients of מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense would be that even value-holiness can be disqualified by a טבול יום, so the ברייתא is no problem. The משנה separates two stages. When the owner dedicates the ingredients, there is only מעילה. Only after they go into a כלי שרת can they be disqualified by a טבול יום, a מחוסר כפורים, or לינה. This shows that value-holiness alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say', which brings up a possible answer in order to reject it.
One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property.
Made holy by being placed in a כלי שרת, a holy vessel.
Someone who has immersed but has not yet brought the offering that completes his purification.
Being left overnight, which disqualifies holy items.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two stages. Dedicating the ingredients by speech already brings liability for מעילה. Being disqualified by a טבול יום starts only when they are put into a vessel.

phrases.english: And if you would say

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים מִיפַּסְלִי בִּטְבוּל יוֹם;
phrases.english: all items with holiness of value are disqualified by a טבול יום;
but didn't we learn in a משנה:
Meal offerings: one is liable for misusing them from when they are dedicated;
once they were made holy in a vessel,
they become able to be disqualified by a טבול יום
and by a מחוסר כפורים and by being left overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כׇּל קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים מִיפַּסְלִי בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible escape from the challenge in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible defense that all קדושת דמים items can be disqualified by a טבול יום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה in מעילה links this disqualification to being made holy in a vessel, not to dedication alone.

steps.title: The inference from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה draws the inference: only after being made holy in a vessel are מנחות disqualified by a טבול יום. Before that, they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were made holy in a vessel, yes. If they were not made holy in a vessel, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה spells out what the משנה implies and finishes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties disqualification by a טבול יום to the vessel. So before the vessel, when the ingredients have only קדושת דמים, a טבול יום cannot disqualify them. That brings back the challenge: since incense can be disqualified this way, it must have more than קדושת דמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Aramaic for 'yes'.
Aramaic for 'no'.

steps.whatToRemember: Value-holiness alone is not disqualified by a טבול יום. Only holiness from a כלי שרת is. So the ברייתא about incense in the mortar is a real problem for רב חסדא's claim that incense is only קדושת דמים.

phrases.english: If they were made holy in a vessel, yes,
phrases.notes: Yes, they can be disqualified by a טבול יום.

phrases.english: if they were not made holy in a vessel, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדְשׁוּ בִּכְלִי אִין, לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בִּכְלִי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That קדושת דמים alone is not disqualified by a טבול יום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעילה about מנחות, read for what it implies.

steps.title: רב חסדא pushes back: then it should be disqualified by being left overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges רבה. If leftover incense has קדושת הגוף, it should become disqualified by לינה. Yet the משנה says only items made holy in a vessel are disqualified by לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying? That it has full, built-in holiness? If so, it should be disqualified by being left overnight! Why then did we learn: The handful, the frankincense, the incense, the meal-offering of priests, the meal-offering of the anointed priest, and the meal-offering of libations: one is liable for misusing them from when they are consecrated. Once they are made holy in a vessel, they become fit to be disqualified by a טבול יום, by one lacking atonement, and by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא turns the question back on רבה. He quotes a similar משנה that lists the incense by name, and this time he points to its last word: לינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה argued that the incense must have more than קדושת דמים, because a טבול יום disqualifies it. רב חסדא answers that if it really had קדושת הגוף, it should also be disqualified by being left overnight. The משנה links all three disqualifications to being made holy in a vessel, and the leftover incense was never put in a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of the item itself. The item is holy and is meant to be offered as it is.
Being left overnight, which disqualifies some holy things.
One is liable for מְעִילָה, misusing holy property.
The handful taken from a מִנְחָה and burned on the altar.
Someone who is pure but has not yet brought his atonement offering.

steps.confusionAlert: The speaker has switched. It is now רב חסדא attacking רבה's position, not רבה asking.

phrases.english: Rather, what — it has inherent holiness?!
But if so, let it be disqualified by being left overnight!
Why then did we learn:
The handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
and the meal-offering of priests and the meal-offering of the anointed priest,
phrases.notes: The "anointed priest" is the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and the meal-offering of libations —
one is liable for misusing them from when they are consecrated;
once they were made holy in a vessel —
they become fit to be disqualified by a טבול יום
and by one lacking atonement, and by being left overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי – קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף הִיא?! אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, תִּיפָּסֵל בְּלִינָה!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רבה's inference with a parallel משנה that explicitly includes incense, focusing on לינה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that leftover incense must have holiness beyond קדושת דמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדושת הגוף should bring disqualification by לינה. The משנה ties לינה to being made holy in a vessel, which never happened to this incense.

steps.title: Only a vessel brings disqualification by being left overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא draws the inference: only items made holy in a vessel are disqualified by לינה. Items not made holy in a vessel are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were made holy in a vessel, yes. If they were not made holy in a vessel, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא spells out exactly what he learns from the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says disqualification begins once the item is made holy in a vessel, before that there is no disqualification by לינה. Leftover incense that was only ground in the mortar would not be disqualified by being left overnight. That suggests it has only קדושת דמים, just as רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Made holy by being placed in a כְּלִי שָׁרֵת (service vessel).
Yes.
No.

phrases.english: If they were made holy in a vessel — yes;
if they were not made holy in a vessel — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדְשׁוּ בִּכְלִי – אִין, לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בִּכְלִי – לָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's proof from the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Leftover incense, never placed in a vessel, is not disqualified by לינה, so it has only קדושת דמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (מעילה) linking disqualification to being made holy in a vessel.

steps.title: Incense is different, because it does not spoil
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the proof from לינה. Incense is never disqualified by being left overnight, because it stays the same all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are bringing a proof from being left overnight? Incense is different, because its form lasts the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רב חסדא. The rule about being left overnight cannot prove anything about incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being left overnight disqualifies things that spoil or change over time. Incense does not change all year, so it would not be disqualified by לינה even if it had קדושת הגוף. So the missing לינה disqualification tells us nothing about what kind of holiness it has.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different.
Since, because.
Its form or condition.

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying incense lacks קדושת הגוף. He is saying לינה simply does not apply to incense, so it cannot be used as a test.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are talking about being left overnight?
Incense is different,
since its form lasts throughout the whole year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִינָה קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי קְטוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's proof from לינה in steps 5–6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from לינה. The טבול יום argument still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Incense is an exception to לינה because it never spoils, so the absence of לינה proves nothing.

steps.title: Back to the original problem: where did the holiness go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the basic difficulty remains. Either way, the question comes back: if leftover public offerings had real holiness, how could they lose it through redemption?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult: the holiness that was in them, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back from the back-and-forth. The original problem has still not been solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה showed that the incense has holiness beyond קדושת דמים, since a טבול יום disqualifies it. Whatever the status of the incense, the original question about redeeming leftover offerings comes right back. Something with real holiness should not be able to lose it simply by being redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, regardless.
Where did it go?

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult:
The holiness that was in them — where did it go?
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא's question from before this section, about how leftover offerings could be redeemed, coming back now.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם קַשְׁיָא: וְכִי קְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁבָּהֶן לְהֵיכָן הָלְכָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's דחיה, returns to רב חסדא's original question of where the holiness of the redeemed leftovers went.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of redeeming leftover incense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the incense had real holiness, redemption should not be able to remove it.

steps.title: The court makes a silent condition
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the בית דין silently makes a condition on public offerings. If they are needed, they are fully holy. If not, they are holy only for their value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The court silently makes a condition about them. If they are needed, they are needed. If not, they will be for their value.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question of where the holiness went. אביי challenges this answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When public items like incense are made holy, the בית דין has an unspoken condition in mind. If the item ends up being used, it has full holiness. If it is left over, it was only ever holy for its value. So redeeming leftover incense does not remove any real holiness: looking back, it only ever had קדושת דמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The court's intent makes a silent condition.
They were needed (for offerings).
For their value. They can be sold and the money used for offerings.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, leftover incense can be redeemed because of the בית דין's silent condition: whatever is not needed was only ever holy for its value. אביי challenges this in steps 10 and 12.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of לב בית דין מתנה explains how public holy property can be redeemed. This principle is used in other places too.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The heart of the court makes a condition about them:
phrases.notes: Literally "the heart": the condition is in the court's mind and is never said out loud.

phrases.english: if they are needed, they are needed;
and if not, they will be for their value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conditional holiness: a silent stipulation by the בית דין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The incense was fully holy, so redemption would have to remove real holiness, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the בית דין's condition, leftover incense was only holy for its value from the start, so it can be redeemed.

steps.title: אביי Quotes רבה's Own Rule Against Him
steps.stepSummary: אביי reminds רבה that רבה himself ruled that a male animal dedicated for its value becomes fully holy (קדושת הגוף). So how can the בית דין's condition keep public offerings holy only for their value?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But aren't you, Master, the one who said that if someone dedicates a male animal for its value, it automatically becomes holy with real, bodily holiness?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's answer from step 9 by quoting a different ruling of רבה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה ruled that an animal fit for the altar cannot stay holy only for its money value. Once it is dedicated, its own body becomes holy. If that is true, the בית דין's silent condition should not work, because the animals and the incense are fit to be offered and should become fully holy anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: He dedicated (something to the בית המקדש)
A male animal, fit to be brought as an offering
For its value, meaning only its money value is holy
Real holiness of the object itself, not just of its money value

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of holiness. קדושת דמים means only the money value is holy, so the item can be redeemed. קדושת הגוף means the item itself is holy and cannot simply be redeemed.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rabba):
But isn't it the Master who said:
phrases.notes: "Master" is a polite way of saying "you." אביי means רבה himself.

phrases.english: If one dedicated a male animal for its value,
it is holy with holiness of its body!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אביי, והא מר הוא דאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 9, which used the בית דין's silent condition, by quoting רבה's own contrary ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim in step 9 that the בית דין's condition can keep public offerings holy only for their value.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה himself holds that something fit for the altar becomes fully holy even when dedicated only for its value. So a condition limiting it to value-holiness should not work.

steps.title: It Depends on What Value It Was Dedicated For
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that his ruling applies only when the animal was dedicated for the value of an עולה. The בית דין's condition is like dedicating it for the value of נסכים, which does not make the animal fully holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. That ruling is where he said "for the value of a burnt-offering." This case is where he said "for the value of wine offerings."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself by showing that his two rulings talk about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal is dedicated for the value of an עולה, the animal itself could be that עולה, so its body becomes holy. If it is dedicated for the value of נסכים, the animal itself can never be נסכים, so only its money is holy. The בית דין's condition works like the second case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources are talking about different cases
A burnt-offering, fully burned on the altar
Wine offerings poured on the altar together with sacrifices

steps.whatToRemember: An animal dedicated for its value becomes fully holy only if it could itself be used for that purpose (an עולה). If it was dedicated for something it can never be (נסכים), only its value is holy.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this (my ruling) is where he said "for the value of a burnt-offering,"
that (the court's condition) is where he said "for the value of wine offerings."

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא; הא דאמר לדמי עולה, הא דאמר לדמי נסכים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's קשיא in step 10 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): the two rulings apply to different kinds of dedication.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal fit for the altar becomes fully holy whenever it is dedicated for its value, so the בית דין's condition cannot work.
steps.terutzMaskana: It becomes fully holy only when dedicated for a purpose it can itself serve (an עולה). The court's condition is like dedicating for נסכים, which leaves only value-holiness.

steps.title: אביי Begins a Challenge from the Lost Yom Kippur Offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a new challenge to רבה from a ברייתא about the פר and שעיר of יום הכפורים that were lost and replaced with others. The ruling of the ברייתא continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection: The bull and goat of יום הכפורים that were lost, and he set aside others in their place...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. אביי begins quoting a ברייתא, and the actual ruling and attack come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far only the case is given: the special יום הכפורים offerings were lost and replaced. The ברייתא will go on to say what happens to the original animals if they are found. That ruling will test רבה's idea of the בית דין's silent condition.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull and the goat brought as special offerings
The Day of Atonement
He set aside (an animal for an offering)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
The bull and goat of Yom Kippur
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place,

steps.triggerLanguage: איתיביה אביי: פר ושעיר של יום הכפורים שאבדו והפריש אחרים תחתיהם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה defended his silent-condition idea in step 11, אביי opens a new attack on it from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim (step 9) that the בית דין silently makes public offerings holy only for their value when they are not needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only partly given here. The ברייתא about lost and replaced יום הכפורים offerings will be used to show a ruling that does not fit the silent condition. The full ruling comes in the next section.
